section_summary: This section contains the concluding portions of a Japanese official monograph on outlying minor islands, examining the geography, history, and legal jurisdiction of Marcus Island, Parece Vela, the Liancourt Rocks (Takeshima), and Dagelet Island (Ulleungdo). It also preserves U.S. Political Adviser Despatch No. 1311 transmitting a formal petition from the Hokkaido Towns and Villages Council to General Douglas MacArthur requesting the return of the Habomai Islands, Kunashiri, and Etorofu from Soviet military occupation. Finally, it includes Despatch No. 1313 and an extensive August 1946 SCAP Civil Information and Education Section survey report listing designated historic sites, scenic spots, and natural history preserves across Japanese prefectures.

subfiles.about: A monograph detailing the geography, history, resources, and jurisdictional status of Marcus Island, Parece Vela, the Liancourt Rocks, and Dagelet Island.
subfiles.summary: This monograph reviews the geography, discovery, settlement, and administrative status of Japan's outlying oceanic and Japan Sea islands. It documents Japanese governance of Marcus Island and Parece Vela in the Pacific Ocean alongside historical European and American visits. It also traces early records and map designations for the Liancourt Rocks (Takeshima) and Dagelet Island (Ulleungdo), concluding with a reproduction of Nagakubo Sekisui's 1775 map.
subfiles.title: Minor Islands Adjacent to Japan Proper: Minor Islands in the Pacific and Minor Islands in the Japan Sea

subfiles.about: A transmittal despatch forwarding to the Department of State a Japanese petition requesting the restoration of islands adjacent to Hokkaido.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwarding a petition to General MacArthur requesting the return of Habomai, Shikotan, Kunashiri, and Etorofu to Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1311: Transmittal of a Petition for the Restoration to Japan of Certain Islands Adjacent to Hokkaido

subfiles.about: A petition submitted to General MacArthur requesting the restoration to Japanese sovereignty of the Habomai Islands, Kunashiri, and Etorofu.
subfiles.from: Chairman of the Hokkaido Towns and Villages Council
subfiles.summary: The Hokkaido Towns and Villages Council petitions General MacArthur for the return of the Habomai Islands, Etorofu, and Kunashiri from Soviet occupation. The petition cites the 1854 and 1875 Russo-Japanese treaties, continuous Japanese habitation, and vital dependence on rich regional fisheries for the national protein supply. It also underscores the hardship and family separation experienced by thousands of Japanese inhabitants currently confined on or displaced from the islands.
subfiles.title: Petition to General Douglas MacArthur for the Restoration to Japan of Certain Islands Adjacent to Hokkaido
subfiles.to: General of the Army Douglas MacArthur, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: A transmittal despatch forwarding copies of a SCAP Civil Information and Education Section report on Japanese historic sites and preserves.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmitting five copies of a SCAP report listing historic sites, scenic spots, and natural history preserves in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1313: Transmittal of a Report Containing a List of Historic Sites, Scenic Spots and Natural History Preserves in Japan

subfiles.about: A comprehensive administrative survey and inventory of registered historic sites, scenic spots, and natural history preserves throughout Japan.
subfiles.from: Civil Information and Education Section, Analysis and Research Division, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: This report reviews the Japanese legislative history and administrative apparatus created since the Meiji era to protect notable localities and wildlife. It presents summary national and prefectural statistics covering 1,943 designated historic sites, scenic spots, and natural history preserves as of December 1944. Detailed inventories sequentially catalogue designated properties across Japanese prefectures from Hokkaido to Fukui, recording classification types, dates, administrative authorities, and historical associations.
subfiles.title: List of Historic Sites, Scenic Spots, and Natural History Preserves in Japan (Serial Number: R-231-CR-E-1)
